title: Strict logarithmic Jacobian criterion
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be locally Noetherian fs log schemes and let $X\to S$, $Y\to S$ be log smooth [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Let $h:X\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism of log schemes which is strict: its source log structure is the pullback of the target log structure. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, with image $\bar y$ in $Y$, and write $k$ for the residue field of $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The relative logarithmic differential module $\omega_f$ is generated over $\mathcal O_X$ by $du$ for regular functions and $d\log m$ for log sections, with additivity, the Leibniz rule, $d\log(mm^{\prime})=d\log m+d\log m^{\prime}$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and vanishing of $du$ and $d\log m$ for sections pulled back from the base. If the natural map $$k\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}}\omega_{Y/S,\bar y}\longrightarrow k\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}}\omega_{X/S,\bar x}$$ is injective, then the underlying scheme morphism $h$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $\bar x$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, strictness and the Jacobian criterion attributed there to Kato 1988, 3.12.

proof.text: Put $E=h^*\omega_{Y/S}$, $F=\omega_{X/S}$ and let $u:E\to F$ send $da$ to $d(h^*a)$ and $d\log m$ to $d\log h^\flat m$. The logarithmic calculus gives finite locally free modules. Choose strict etale neighborhoods at the given point on which they have finite bases. The hypothesis says the resulting finite matrix has full column rank over the geometric residue field, hence also over the residue field of the point on the chosen neighborhood: scalar extension by a field is faithful, as a nonzero vector remains nonzero. Apply the finite-free residue-localization lemma to shrink this neighborhood so that $u$ has a left inverse $r:F\to E$. Finite sections and the inverse identities spread from an etale stalk to an etale neighborhood by the definition of that stalk (only finitely many entries and equalities occur). Denote this etale neighborhood by $U\to X$ and replace $X$ by $U$ for the following lifting calculation. Log smoothness over $S$ and the calculus persist under this localization.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed p.138; agent expansion of the strict logarithmic Jacobian argument into infinitesimal lifts.

proof.text: The map $h:U\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation. Indeed the calculus gives this for $U\to S$ and $Y\to S$. Work over a common affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, and affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$, $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset U$ with $h(\operatorname{Spec}C)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine-open finite-presentation theorem gives that $B$ and $C$ are finitely presented over $R$, so $B$ is of finite type over $R$. The intermediate-algebra finite-presentation theorem applied to $R\to B\to C$ gives that $C$ is finitely presented over $B$. These neighborhoods cover $U$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed p.138; agent expansion of the strict logarithmic Jacobian argument into infinitesimal lifts.

proof.text: Take any affine square-zero thickening $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, ideal $\mathcal I$, and scheme maps $a_0:T_0\to U$, $b:T\to Y$ with $ha_0=bi$. Endow $T$ with $b^*M_Y$ and $T_0$ with its pullback. These are fine log structures on arbitrary test schemes: a finite integral chart for $M_Y$ pulls back to the same prelog chart followed by association with the units. Since $h$ is strict, $a_0$ has the canonical log map, and $i$ is strict. Concretely $b^*M_Y$ is the sheafification of the pushout $b^{-1}M_Y\oplus_{\beta^{-1}\mathcal O_T^\times}\mathcal O_T^\times$; a compatible map out is determined by its maps on the two factors. Apply the calculus to $U\to S$. Etale locally on $T$ there is a log lift $a:T\to U$ of $a_0$ over $S$. It need not yet be a lift over $Y$. All subsequent calculations take place on this covering, which suffices for the etale-local smoothness criterion.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed p.138; agent expansion of the strict logarithmic Jacobian argument into infinitesimal lifts.

proof.text: The two log maps $ha$ and $b$ to $Y$ are lifts over $S$ of the same map $ha_0$. The torsor assertion for $Y\to S$ gives their unique difference $\delta:(ha_0)^*\omega_{Y/S}\to\mathcal I$, with the sign convention $ha=b+\delta$. Pull back $r$ along $a_0$ and put $\epsilon=-\delta\circ a_0^*r:a_0^*\omega_{U/S}\to\mathcal I$. The torsor assertion for $U\to S$ defines a new lift $a'=a+\epsilon$. For a regular function $v$ on $Y$, the change in $(ha)^\sharp(v)$ is $\epsilon(dh^*v)$; for a log section $m$ it is multiplication by $1+\epsilon(d\log h^\flat m)$. Thus the difference of $ha'$ from $ha$ is $\epsilon\circ a_0^*u=-\delta$, since $ru=1$. Additivity follows directly from $(1+s)(1+t)=1+s+t$ for $s,t\in\mathcal I$. Consequently $ha'=b$ both on functions and on log sections, and $a'|_{T_0}=a_0$. This proves existence of solutions etale locally for every test square, with no Noetherian hypothesis on the tests.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed p.138; agent expansion of the strict logarithmic Jacobian argument into infinitesimal lifts.

proof.text: Apply the etale-local infinitesimal smoothness lemma to $U\to Y$, using its local finite presentation from Step 2 and the lifts constructed in Steps 3--4. It is smooth. The pointwise etale-source locality theorem, applied to $U\to X$ and $h:X\to Y$, implies that the original $h$ is smooth at the image of our chosen point of $U$. By the meaning of smooth at a point, there is an open neighborhood of $\bar x$ on which $h$ is smooth. No assertion that an arbitrary etale-local lift automatically descends was used: that descent is exactly the content of the new general scheme lemma.
